work_package: C5-FFC-WRAPPER (early TOPP bundle, wave 3a), reconciled with the completed algorithm of B7-FFAP-FEATURES after both merged; src/cli/tools/feature_finder_centroided.rs, this manifest, the tests and the support document pass to B10 in wave 4
scope: The FeatureFinderCentroided TOPP wrapper end to end: registration and -write_ini, the source loading options, the empty-input, per-peak ion-mobility and profile branches in source order, the seed load, the FAIMS refusal of decision D5, the error mapping of the algorithm's failures, the algorithm run itself with -threads reaching its seed loop, and the post-algorithm annotation and clean-up (primary MS run path, unique ids, the QUANTITATION processing record, hull and subordinate reduction). TOPP_FeatureFinderCentroided_1 is compared decoded against the retained expectation and measured against the C++ Release build. Not in scope: the 1e-9 acceptance against the C1 oracle outputs of FFC_seeds, FFC_asymmetric and FFC_debug5 and the -algorithm:fit:max_iterations boundary sweep (B10), and the FAIMS closure (B11).
method: The tool is transcribed from the pinned topp source and exercised through the built executable in a temporary working directory, because the FeatureFinderCentroided_1 INI sets log=TOPP.log. Every wrapper branch is compared with a C++ run of the same command against the product SDK: the planned regressions in the C1 oracle (../oracle/topp-early-bundle) and the branch-order cases this package added (../oracle/ffc-wrapper-c5), each executed twice and reproduced. Synthetic inputs are not committed: the tests re-derive them from the retained FeatureFinderCentroided_1_input.mzML by the rule the oracle manifests record and check the derived bytes against the SHA-1 of the file the C++ tool read, whose SHA-256 is recorded below. The runs that reach the algorithm are additionally measured against the optimised C++ build openms4-release-bc9cc12-c19e494-174b576 on an IBMI Linux node under the same environment shape (env -i, OPENMS_DATA_PATH, per-case scratch cwd); that build's featureXML reproduces the Debug oracle to within 9.1e-11 relative, and the measured port-to-Release gaps are recorded in docs/TOPP_FEATURE_FINDER_CENTROIDED_SUPPORT.md.
evidence_tier: tier 1 (executed differential) for every asserted exit code, diagnostic and absence of output, for the -write_ini defaults, and for the feature output: the product SDK Debug core 4fdec46 for the oracle cases, and the Release build openms4-release-bc9cc12-c19e494-174b576 for the numeric comparison; tier 3 (source review of FeatureFinderCentroided.cpp at topp 174b576) for the registration details

derived_inputs_note: Derived from tests/data/mzml_mobility/FeatureFinderCentroided_1_input.mzML inside each test's temporary directory, never committed. sha256 is the file the C++ tool read (recorded in the oracle manifest named below); sha1 is what the test asserts about the bytes it derived, which pins them to that file.

derived_inputs.name: profile/FeatureFinderCentroided_1_input.mzML
derived_inputs.rule: every 'MS:1000525 spectrum representation' cvParam replaced by 'MS:1000128 profile spectrum' (112 spectra)

derived_inputs.name: profile_before_1000525/FeatureFinderCentroided_1_input.mzML
derived_inputs.rule: an unindented 'MS:1000128 profile spectrum' cvParam line inserted before every 'MS:1000525 spectrum representation' line (112 spectra)

derived_inputs.name: im_peak_ms1.mzML
derived_inputs.rule: binaryDataArrayList count 2 -> 3 and a third uncompressed 32-bit 'MS:1002816 mean ion mobility array' (UO:0000028 millisecond) of defaultArrayLength values 0.5 appended to every spectrum (112 MS1 spectra)

derived_inputs.name: im_peak_ms1_nounit.mzML
derived_inputs.rule: as im_peak_ms1.mzML but the ion mobility cvParam carries no unit attributes

derived_inputs.name: faims_one_cv.mzML
derived_inputs.rule: an unindented scan-level 'MS:1001581 FAIMS compensation voltage' cvParam (value -45, UO:0000218 volt) inserted after every <scan> line (112 spectra)

derived_inputs.name: faims_two_cv.mzML
derived_inputs.rule: as faims_one_cv.mzML, alternating -45 (even spectrum index) and -60 (odd index)

derived_inputs.name: im_peak_profile.mzML
derived_inputs.rule: im_peak_ms1.mzML with every 'MS:1000525 spectrum representation' cvParam replaced by 'MS:1000128 profile spectrum'

derived_inputs.name: first_profile_only/FeatureFinderCentroided_1_input.mzML
derived_inputs.rule: the first 'MS:1000525 spectrum representation' cvParam replaced by 'MS:1000128 profile spectrum'

derived_inputs.name: later_profile_only/FeatureFinderCentroided_1_input.mzML
derived_inputs.rule: every 'MS:1000525 spectrum representation' cvParam but the first replaced by 'MS:1000128 profile spectrum'

derived_inputs.name: negative_intensities.mzML
derived_inputs.rule: the sign bit of every little-endian 32-bit float in each 'MS:1000515 intensity array' <binary> set (all 3084 values were positive); base64 re-encoded, encodedLength unchanged

derived_inputs.name: faims_partial_cv.mzML
derived_inputs.rule: an unindented scan-level 'MS:1001581 FAIMS compensation voltage' cvParam (value -45, UO:0000218 volt) inserted after the <scan> line of every even-indexed spectrum (56 of 112)

upstream_test_definition: OpenMS4-tests/packages/test-data/topp/CMakeLists.txt lines 425-428 (TOPP_FeatureFinderCentroided_1 and its FuzzyDiff comparison) and lines 83-85 (TOPPWRITEINI_<tool>)
determinism: The wrapper passes ToolContext::thread_policy to the algorithm's seed loop, whose results keep seed order, and every later step is serial. -threads 0, 1, 2, 4 and 8 write byte-identical featureXML, unique ids included, which tests/topp_feature_finder_centroided.rs::the_output_is_byte_identical_at_every_thread_count asserts; every other assertion here is exact.
